narrations.en: Step 60 (Final Step): The visual proof is complete! Starting from the starting condition of 'divergence to infinity of a function (AP)', which observes the slope (average rate of change) of the secant line or the sum of the areas of divided rectangles as the limit in the curve on the coordinate plane, which was the starting condition, through the secant connecting two points on the curve and the geometric auxiliary line that constructs a right triangle (delta It was clearly confirmed that the calculus conclusion that the relationship between the instantaneous rate of change (slope of the tangent) and the definite integral area at 'divergence (AP)' is strictly established holds true. The key point to remember here is that just because a function is continuous at a point does not always mean it is differentiable! Like the peak point of an absolute value graph, if the left and right differential coefficients are different, even if they are continuous, they cannot be differentiated because the tangent line is not determined as one. Finally, ask a deeper question. How can two seemingly completely different geometric problems, differentiation (slope of a tangent line) and integration (area under a curve), become completely inversely arithmetic with just one 'fundamental theorem of calculus'?
